title: Operator metering and trace sprint notes
body:
Purpose: quick working guide and sprint checklist for "operator metering" — the minimal metric + trace surface we want in place for the next two rollouts: (1) canary quantized models, (2) multi-tenant dedicated pools. This is intentionally operator-focused: concise panels, cheap probes, and trace anchors that help an oncall engineer answer the three questions in <5 minutes: is it a capacity problem, a model regression, or a routing/fallback event?

Audience: oncall SREs, deployment engineers, product owners for Dedicated, and solutions engineers running customer rollouts.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Make the default investigation path reproduceable: single dashboard, 3 trace anchors, and a one-page runbook.
- Reduce query cost for exploratory debugging by 30% via coarser rollups + microprobe approach.
- Ensure cold-cache and KV-eviction events are visible in the first 3 heatmap buckets.

Scope (this doc):
- metric definitions for model-serving/operator surface (throughput, latency slices, error types, cache hit/warmth)
- trace anchor points and sampling policy recommendations
- dashboard layout notes and small-panel wireframes for operator workflow
- sprint checklist: instrumentation, QA, rollout, and postmortem anchors

1) Core metrics (definitions and measurement hints)
- request.count (unit: requests/min) — increment at request ingress. Tag by route/model/tenant/region. Use low cardinality for tenant (tenant_tier: free/paid/enterprise) for most panels.
- request.user_latency_ms (unit: p50/p90/p99) — measure on response completion. Break down into: ingress-ms, scheduling-ms, runtime-ms, kv-lookup-ms, network-ms. If you cannot instrument per-phase, runtime-ms is most important for inference regression detection.
- token.generated.count (unit: tokens/sec) — emitted from runtime; helpful for token-economics. Roll up by model family for cost buckets.
- runtime.cpu_util_pct and gpu_util_pct (unit: pct) — sampled at 10s; correlate with scheduling-ms.
- kv.cache.hit_rate and kv.cache.warmth_index (unit: pct and 0-1) — define warm if prefix seen within 10s window; warmth_index is fraction of requests with a warm prefix. Suggest asymmetric tagging: cold vs partial-warm vs warm.
- model.fallback.count (unit: count) — instances where routing fallback to alternative model variant occurs; tag by original_model and fallback_model.
- generation.error.class (unit: categorical) — categorize error taxonomy: model-timeout, token-overflow, oom, invalid-input, serialization. Use short codes for dashboards (MT, TO, OOM, INV).
- session.kv_eviction_events (unit: count) — increments when the per-session KV is evicted; useful to detect capacity churn.
- batch.size.dist (unit: histogram) — track distribution of batch sizes per instance; helps tune batching policies.

Measurement notes: prefer low-cardinality tags on high-frequency metrics (latency, count). For high-cardinality signals (per-user prompt id, long prompt hashes) use sampled traces or a separate debug stream.

2) Trace anchors and sampling policy
- Anchor A: ingress->scheduler->selected-instance. Purpose: identity routing and scheduling delays. Sample 0.5% of requests globally, increase to 10% when request.user_latency_ms > p95 threshold.
- Anchor B: runtime token loop -> kv fetch -> kv hit/miss branch. Purpose: surface KV hotness and per-token stalls. Sample 1% baseline for heavy-generating requests, escalate on kv.cache.warmth_index drop.
- Anchor C: fallback decision span (model selection + transform). Purpose: capture decision log when fallback occurs. Sample all fallback.count events (sample rate 100% for fallbacks).

Sampling budget: aim for 1k traces/day per region baseline for production services; allocate additional budget for active rollouts (10k/day region). Use severity-weighted sampling: more likely to keep traces with error flags or latency > p99.

Trace enrichments (must be present on spans): route, model_version, instance_id, tenant_tier, generation_length, kv_prefix_hash (lightweight) and probe_id when applicable. Avoid raw prompt text in traces (PII risk).

3) Dashboard layout (operator-first)
- Top row (red/amber/green status): overall QPS, global p95 latency, current error-rate (5m), KV warmth index. Each tile links to the detailed panel via a trace anchor.
- Second row (fast triage panels): per-model p95 and p99 latency (sparkline), fallback rate (last 1h), average batch size, instance util (GPU/CPU heatmap).
- Third row (cost & capacity): tokens/min by model, estimated token-cost (USD per minute) for active models, burst queue length.
- Fourth row (deep-dive widgets): small linked list of recent traces (Anchor A/B/C), session-replay snippets (no raw prompt), and a mini-heatmap showing per-instance cold starts and KV evictions.

Panel heuristics: keep each panel to one query, pre-aggregated rollups. Use derived fields: latency_slice = bucket(latency_ms, [0,50,200,500,1000,inf]) to avoid expensive quantile queries on the dashboard.

Wireframe notes (operator clicks):
- Click QPS -> opens route-level page filtered by last 15 minutes, shows per-tenant QPS and top-k routes.
- Click KV Warmth -> opens microprobe view showing prefix collision map and eviction timeline.
- Click fallback -> opens runbook with fallback decision trace examples and quick rollback link.

4) Sprint checklist (instrumentation -> validation -> rollout)
- Instrumentation (owner: Priya): emit new metrics with standardized tags (model, route, tenant_tier, region). Add span tags for trace enrichments.
- Local QA (owner: Luis): generate synthetic traffic covering warm/cold/partial-warm prefixes, batched and single-token streams. Validate panels in staging.
- Canary rollout (owner: Maya): enable 1% traffic on production dedicated pool with elevated trace sampling. Run 48h smoke window.
- Post-canal validation: run probe-driven checks (warmth_index threshold, p99 < baseline+20%). If any failure, auto-escalate to oncall.

5) Cost-awareness and telemetry budget
- Default dashboards must use pre-aggregated metrics (minute rollups). Avoid on-the-fly trace-driven quantiles unless operator explicitly requests them.
- Implement adaptive sampling: when trace budget > 80% use severity-weighted downsampling; when < 20% remaining, restrict sampling to fallback and error traces only.

6) Runbook snippets (quick answers)
- When p99 spikes but GPU util low -> check scheduling-ms and batch.size.dist: likely cold instances or request fanout.
- When p99 spikes and GPU util high -> suspect model regression; check model.fallback.count and generation.error.class for OOM or timeouts.
- When KV warmth drops -> look for redeploys, instance churn, or deployment of new tokenizer (prefix hash mismatch). Common cause: aggressive eviction policy after memory pressure.

7) Open questions / TODOs
- Decide canonical warm-window (10s vs 30s) for kv.cache.warmth_index. Shorter window catches microbursts but is noisy.
- Should batch.size.dist be sampled per-instance or per-pool? Per-instance gives better visibility but higher cardinality.
- Integrate a lightweight probe that replays last-known-warm prefixes at low QPS to keep warm for VIP tenants — legal/consent implications?
- Define exact cost attribution formula for tokens across Dedicated vs Hosted models (is token-cost proportional to runtime-ms or tokens generated?).

Next steps (next 2 weeks):
- Priya: land metric schema PR, add tags and doc comments (due 2025-11-20).
- Luis: staging dashboard and probe harness (due 2025-11-28).
- Maya: canary plan + trace budget gating (due 2025-12-05).
- Follow-up sync: bring initial dashboards to the Observability weekly on 2025-12-01 for feedback.

Appendix: short examples (promql style hints)
- QPS by model: sum(rate(request_count{job=\"inference\", model=~\".*\"}[1m])) by (model)
- KV warmth (minute): avg_over_time(kv_warmth_index[1m]) by (pool)
- Fallback rate: increase(model_fallback_count[5m]) / increase(request_count[5m])

Notes to self: keep this doc small and actionable. We will expand to a full "instrumentation contract" once the sprint proves the operator flow works in production.

End of working notes.
